name: research_rag
system_prompt: You are an autonomous research agent. Answer the user's question by searching and reading sources with the available retrieval tools, cross-checking claims, and citing where each fact came from. Prefer read-only search and retrieval; produce a concise, sourced answer.

tool_descriptions.web_search: Run a search over the internal knowledge base and wiki for a free-text query and return a ranked list of hits, each with a title, url, and a short snippet of surrounding context. Use this as a first, broad pass to discover which sources and documents are even relevant to a topic before retrieving specific passages, especially when you do not yet know which source or document to target directly with retrieve_docs or read_file.
tool_descriptions.fetch_url: Fetch a specific url and return a plain-text excerpt of the page's main content, up to an optional character limit. Use this once web_search or a prior result has surfaced a specific url worth reading in full, to get its actual content rather than relying on the short snippet from the search results -- the excerpt strips navigation and boilerplate so you see the substantive text first.
tool_descriptions.retrieve_docs: Semantically retrieve the top-k most relevant passages for a query from one named indexed source, each returned with a relevance score. Use this instead of web_search when you already know which source is likely to contain the answer and want ranked passages directly, or when a keyword search under grep would miss a passage that is topically relevant but does not literally contain the query terms.
tool_descriptions.read_file: Read a specific document or file from a named source and return an excerpt of its contents. Use this once retrieve_docs or web_search has identified a specific document worth reading in full -- the returned excerpt includes the document's key points and last-updated timestamp, which is useful both for citing the source accurately and for judging how current the information is likely to be.
tool_descriptions.grep: Search for a regex or literal pattern across all of a source's documents and return matching lines together with their file and line-number locations. Use this when you are looking for an exact phrase, identifier, or term that should appear verbatim -- a decision name, a ticket number, a specific quote -- rather than a broader semantically-related passage, which retrieve_docs is better suited for.
tool_descriptions.list_sources: List the available sources and indexes that can be searched or retrieved from, each with its document count and the timestamp it was last indexed, optionally filtered by a substring over source names. Use this at the start of an investigation when you are not sure which sources exist or are relevant, or to sanity-check that a source you expect to search is actually indexed and reasonably current before relying on its absence as evidence.
tool_descriptions.summarize_findings: Summarize the passages gathered so far for a topic into a short synthesized answer with inline citations, optionally bounded to a maximum word count. Use this once you have retrieved passages from multiple sources and are ready to consolidate them into a coherent narrative, rather than presenting the raw passages -- but only after cross-checking for contradictions between sources, since this tool synthesizes what you feed it and does not itself resolve disagreements.
tool_descriptions.write_answer: Save the research agent's drafted final answer for a topic, including its inline source citations, as the deliverable for this investigation. Call this only once as the last step, after summarize_findings has produced a synthesized answer you have reviewed and are confident is well-supported and accurately cited -- this is the terminal action of the research task, not an intermediate checkpoint to call repeatedly while still gathering passages.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters of the excerpt to return.

query.description: Query to semantically retrieve passages for.

filter.description: Optional substring filter over source names.

topic.description: Topic to synthesize the gathered passages for.

max_words.description: Maximum length of the summary in words.

result_templates.web_search:
web_search query={topic}: {count0} hits
  1. {title} — https://wiki.internal/{doc} ({source})
     snippet: ...discusses {topic} and its impact; last edited {t0}...
  2. {title_b} — https://wiki.internal/{doc_b} ({source})
     snippet: ...notes on {topic}; relevance score {relevance_pct}...
  3. {title} — https://wiki.internal/{doc_c} ({source})
     snippet: ...background context for {topic}...
result_templates.fetch_url:
fetched https://wiki.internal/{doc} ({source}) [{count0} chars]
"{title}"
> On {t0} the team reviewed {topic}. The document states that the change
> was rolled out in stages and that follow-up items remain open. See also
> the linked {source} entry for the full timeline and owners.
result_templates.retrieve_docs:
top-{count0} passages for {topic} from {source}:
  [score={relevance_pct}] {doc}: "{topic} was first raised in the {source} thread and later documented here."
  [score={score_pct}] {doc_b}: "the decision on {topic} was ratified after review; owners were assigned."
  [score={score_pct}] {doc_c}: "open questions about {topic} remain tracked in the backlog."
result_templates.read_file:
read {doc} from {source} ({count0} lines)
---
# {title}
This document covers {topic}. Last updated {t0}.
Key points:
  - background and motivation for {topic}
  - the agreed approach and its owners
  - open follow-ups still being tracked
---
result_templates.grep:
grep pattern in {source}: {count0} matches
  {doc}:{n0}: mentions {topic} in the summary section
  {doc_b}:{n1}: TODO revisit {topic} after the next review
  {doc_c}:{n2}: see also the {source} discussion on {topic}
result_templates.summarize_findings:
summary for {topic} (confidence {relevance_pct}):
{topic} is documented across {count0} sources. The consensus from {source}
and the linked {doc} is that the matter is understood and tracked, with a
few open follow-ups. Citations: {doc} ({source}); {title}.
result_templates.write_answer: answer saved for {topic}: {n0} words, {n1} citations, draft v{n2} (checkpoint {t0}). sources cited: {source}, {source_b}.
result_templates.empty_search: web_search query={topic}: no results found in {source}. Try broadening the query or listing sources first.
result_templates.default: retrieval result for {topic}: {count0} passages from {source}; top doc {doc} (score {relevance_pct}) as of {t0}

objective_template: {verb} what the sources say about {topic}: gather the relevant passages and produce a concise, cited answer.
followup_templates: which {source} entries mention {topic}, and what do they say?
can you read {doc} and pull the key passage on {topic}?
are there any contradictions between sources about {topic}?
what is the single best citation for {topic}?
payload_templates: According to {source}, {topic} was driven primarily by a change first documented in {doc}, which records that roughly {pct0}% of the impact traced back to a single upstream decision [{doc}]. A later review in {source_b} broadly agrees, though it adds {n0} caveats worth flagging [{doc_b}].

The evidence here is mixed. {source} frames {topic} as a process failure and cites {doc} in support, whereas {source_b} attributes it to a tooling gap [{doc_b}]. On balance the {doc} account is better sourced, and it aligns with the timeline recorded in {title}.

A follow-up thread in {source_b} notes that {topic} recurred after the first fix, contradicting the earlier all-clear claimed in {source} [{doc}]. The {title} write-up reconciles the two by distinguishing the initial trigger from the {n0} regressions that followed [{doc_b}].

In short: the {topic} is best explained by {doc} ({source}), corroborated by {title} and partially by {doc_b} ({source_b}). The one open disagreement is scope — {source} reads it as isolated, while {source_b} argues it affected about {pct0}% of downstream flows.

Drafting the answer: the strongest single citation for {topic} is {doc} in {source}, which lays out the sequence directly. Secondary support comes from {doc_b} ({source_b}) and the summary in {title}; {n0} minor points remain unverified and are noted as such.
compaction_summary_template: {verb} what the sources say about {topic}. So far: ran {tool_a}, {tool_b}, and {tool_c}; collected passages from {source} and {doc} and began assembling a cited answer. Coverage is still partial; continuing to gather and reconcile the relevant material.
